Our Home Studio

Minutes from Arlington

Train at Our Home Dojang in Pantego

Lone Star Institute of Taekwondo's main studio sits at 1541 S. Bowen Road in Pantego — a short drive from anywhere in Arlington, and the heart of everything we teach. For more than 15 years, Arlington families have trained here alongside their Pantego neighbors, working through the full curriculum from Little Ninjas and Youth Classes to Adult Classes and Advanced Sparring, Breaking, and Competition.

The studio is led personally by Master David Kestenbaum, a 7th Degree Black Belt certified by the Kukkiwon world headquarters in Seoul and the United States Taekwondo Grandmasters Society. Trained since age 5 and recognized at 24 as one of the youngest Taekwondo Masters in the world, Master Kestenbaum has competed nationally and internationally, trained at the U.S. Olympic Training Center, and holds over 500 trophies and medals — experience he brings to every class, every week. Read his full story.

Our Classes

Every LSIT program is built around the same five tenets and the same certified instructors — just at different ages and stages. Here's what Arlington families can expect at each level.

Ages 3–5

Little Ninjas

A playful first step onto the mat — preschoolers work on balance, listening skills, and using a strong voice. Arlington families can catch this class Tuesday evenings at Cliff Nelson Recreation Center, or join the full weekly schedule at our Pantego studio.

Learn More

Ages 6–17

Youth Classes

Kids and teens build focus, discipline, and practical self-defense in a structured, encouraging setting. Arlington students train through belt-based sessions at Cliff Nelson and Dottie Lynn Recreation Centers, with the option to add extra class days at our Pantego studio.

Learn More

Ages 18+

Adult Classes

A welcoming, beginner-friendly class for adults training for fitness, stress relief, or real self-defense. Adult classes currently run at our Pantego studio, a short drive from anywhere in Arlington, with evening and daytime session options.

Learn More

Sparring • Breaking • Competition

Advanced Classes

Once students reach orange belt, they're eligible for sparring, board breaking, and our competitive team, which trains and competes through the Texas Karate League, Texas State Taekwondo Association, and USA Taekwondo. This track runs at our Pantego studio.

Learn More

Right in Your Arlington Neighborhood

Prefer something closer to home? Lone Star Institute of Taekwondo also teaches focused, belt-based classes at two Arlington recreation centers. These sessions cover core belt training and Little Ninjas — for the full program, including Advanced Sparring and Competition Team, our home studio in Pantego is just minutes away.

The Five Tenets of Taekwondo

예의

Courtesy

Ye-wee

Courtesy (예의, ye-wee) reminds us to show respect in the dojang and beyond through sincere etiquette and kindness.

염치

Integrity

Yom-chee

Integrity (염치, yom-chee) calls for honesty, strong morals, and the courage to do what is right even when it is difficult.

인내

Perseverance

Een-nay

Perseverance (인내, een-nay) is the willingness to keep pushing toward every goal despite obstacles in training or life.

극기

Self Control

Gook-gee

Self control (극기, gook-gee) keeps thoughts, emotions, and actions in balance so we can respond with a steady mind and body.

백절불굴

Indomitable Spirit

Baekjool Boolgool

Indomitable spirit (백절불굴, baekjool boolgool) is to be defeated a hundred times yet never bent — the heart of true strength.
